original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
mayyāsaktamanāḥ pārtha yogaṃ yuñjanmadāśrayaḥ|
asaṃśayaṃ samagraṃ māṃ yathā jñāsyasi tacchṛṇu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: With your mind attached to me (mayy āsakta-manāḥ), Pārtha, practising yoga and taking refuge in me (mad-āśraya), hear how you will know me entirely (samagram) and without doubt.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Opens chapter 7 directly after 6.47 (the one who worships with faith, inner self gone to me, is the most yoked); the verse gives the conditions (mind attached to him, yoga, refuge) and announces the subject: knowing him 'entire' (samagra).

original.text:
jñānaṃ te'haṃ savijñānamidaṃ vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ|
yajjñātvā neha bhūyo'nyajjñātavyamavaśiṣyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I will declare to you, without remainder, this knowledge (jñāna) together with vijñāna; having known it, nothing else remains here to be known.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Commentators divide on the pair jñāna / vijñāna (e.g. knowledge received through teaching vs. its direct realization; or knowledge of the Lord's essential nature vs. knowledge of his distinguishing glories). Paraphrase keeps both words. Stated result (phala): nothing further remains to be known.

original.text:
manuṣyāṇāṃ sahasreṣu kaśicadyatati siddhaye|
yatatāmapi siddhānāṃ kaśicanmāṃ vetti tattvataḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Among thousands of human beings hardly one strives for perfection (siddhi); and even among those who strive and are perfected (siddha), hardly one knows me in truth (tattvataḥ).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'yatatām api siddhānām' is read either as 'among the striving (who count as) perfected' or 'among those who strive, even of the perfected'; either way the verse grades rarity: striving, perfection, knowing him in truth. IAST 'kaśicad/kaśican' is a transliteration artefact of the segment for kaścid/kaścin.

original.text:
bhūmirāpo'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhireva ca|
ahaṅkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtiraṣṭadhā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Earth, water, fire, air, space (kha), mind (manas), intellect (buddhi) and the I-maker (ahaṃkāra): thus is this nature (prakṛti) of mine divided eightfold.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The eightfold list names five elements and three inner faculties as 'my' prakṛti; the verse does not itself say whether the elements meant are gross or subtle. Cross-ref 13.6 is the numbering of this edition (13.5 in editions without the extra verse at the head of ch. 13).

original.text:
apareyamitastvanyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām|
jīvabhūtāṃ mahābāho yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: This is the lower (aparā) [nature]; but know my other, higher nature (parā prakṛti), mighty-armed, which has become the living being (jīva-bhūtā), by which this world is upheld.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'jīvabhūtā' ('which is / has become the living being(s)') is read by commentators either as the principle of life, the knower of the field, or as the souls collectively; the verse itself only calls it the Lord's higher prakṛti by which the world is held up.

original.text:
etadyonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇītyupadhāraya|
ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayastathā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Understand that all beings have these [two natures] as their womb/source (etad-yonīni); I am the origin (prabhava) and likewise the dissolution (pralaya) of the whole world.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyatkiñcidasti dhanañjaya|
mayi sarvamidaṃ protaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: There is nothing whatever higher than me, Dhanaṃjaya; all this is strung on me like clusters of gems (maṇi-gaṇa) on a thread (sūtra).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Image of the thread and gems: everything held on him as its common support.

original.text:
raso'hamapsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śaśisūryayoḥ|
praṇavaḥ sarvavedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am the taste (rasa) in the waters, Kaunteya; I am the light of moon and sun; the syllable Oṃ (praṇava) in all the Vedas, sound (śabda) in space (kha), manhood (pauruṣa) in men.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 7.8–11 name the Lord as the essence or distinguishing quality in each thing (the defining quality of each element, of the Veda, of persons).

original.text:
puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ca tejaścāsmi vibhāvasau|
jīvanaṃ sarvabhūteṣu tapaścāsmi tapasviṣu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And I am the pure fragrance (puṇyo gandhaḥ) in the earth, the radiance (tejas) in fire, the life (jīvana) in all beings, and the austerity (tapas) in ascetics.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
bījaṃ māṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam|
buddhirbuddhimatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Know me, Pārtha, as the eternal seed (bījaṃ sanātanam) of all beings; I am the intelligence (buddhi) of the intelligent, the brilliance (tejas) of the brilliant.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
balaṃ balavatāṃ cāhaṃ kāmarāgavivarjitam|
dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo'smi bharatarṣabha
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of the strong I am the strength that is free of desire and passion (kāma-rāga-vivarjita); in beings I am the desire (kāma) that is not opposed to dharma, bull of the Bharatas.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Distinguishes desire in accord with dharma (identified with the Lord) from desire and passion as such; cf. 3.37 where kāma born of rajas is the enemy.

original.text:
ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasāstāmasāśca ye|
matta eveti tānviddhi natvahaṃ teṣu te mayi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And whatever states/beings (bhāvāḥ) are of sattva, of rajas and of tamas — know that they come from me alone; yet I am not in them: they are in me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'I am not in them, they are in me' — the same asymmetry is developed in 9.4–5.

original.text:
tribhirguṇamayairbhāvairebhiḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat|
mohitaṃ nābhijānāti māmebhyaḥ paramavyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Deluded (mohita) by these three kinds of states made of the guṇas, this whole world does not recognize me, who am beyond them (ebhyaḥ param) and imperishable (avyaya).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
daivī hyeṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā|
māmeva ye prapadyante māyāmetāṃ taranti te
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For this divine (daivī) māyā of mine, made of the guṇas (guṇamayī), is hard to get beyond (duratyayā); those who take refuge in me alone (mām eva prapadyante) cross over this māyā.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse says of māyā only that it is divine, belongs to the Lord, consists of the guṇas, is hard to cross and is crossed by those who take refuge in him; commentators divide on its nature (a power of appearance vs. the guṇa-made prakṛti that conceals the Lord).

original.text:
na māṃ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ|
māyayāpahṛtajñānā āsuraṃ bhāvamāśritāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Evil-doers (duṣkṛtinaḥ), the deluded (mūḍhāḥ), the lowest of men, whose knowledge is carried off by māyā and who resort to the demonic state (āsuraṃ bhāvam), do not take refuge in me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
caturvidhā bhajante māṃ janāḥ sukṛtino'rjuna|
ārto jijñāsurarthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Four kinds of people of good deeds (sukṛtinaḥ) worship me (bhajante), Arjuna: the distressed (ārta), the one who wishes to know (jijñāsu), the seeker of gain (artha-arthin), and the knower (jñānin), bull of the Bharatas.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

tags.stage_native: the four kinds of devotees: ārta, jijñāsu, arthārthin, jñānin

translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'arthārthin' is read as one seeking wealth/prosperity or, more widely, one seeking a desired object.

original.text:
teṣāṃ jñānī nityayukta ekabhakitarviśiṣyate|
priyo hi jñānino'tyarthamahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of these the knower (jñānin), ever yoked (nitya-yukta) and of single devotion (eka-bhakti), is distinguished; for I am exceedingly dear to the knower, and he is dear to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The knower is named foremost as a kind of devotee (knowledge and single devotion joined). IAST 'ekabhakitar' is a transliteration artefact for ekabhaktir. Contrast 9.29 ('none is dear to me') with the mutual dearness stated here.

original.text:
udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tvātmaiva me matam|
āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā māmevānuttamāṃ gatim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: All these are noble (udāra), but the knower I hold to be my very self (ātmā eva me matam); for he, with self yoked (yuktātmā), is established in me alone as the unsurpassed goal.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'jñānī tv ātmaiva me matam' is read as the knower's non-difference from the Lord, or as the knower being as dear to the Lord as his own self / his very life; the verse itself says only that the Lord 'holds' (matam) the knower to be his self. The other three kinds are still called noble.

original.text:
bahūnāṃ janmanāmante jñānavānmāṃ prapadyate|
vāsudevaḥ sarvamiti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: At the end of many births the one who has knowledge (jñānavān) takes refuge in me, [knowing] 'Vāsudeva is all' (vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti); such a great soul (mahātman) is very hard to find.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Kṛṣṇa names himself Vāsudeva. The rarity theme repeats 7.3.

original.text:
kāmaistaistairhṛtajñānāḥ prapadyante'nyadevatāḥ|
taṃ taṃ niyamamāsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those whose knowledge has been carried off by this or that desire (kāma) resort to other deities (anya-devatāḥ), adopting this or that rule of observance (niyama), constrained by their own nature (prakṛti).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitumicchati|
tasya tasyācalāṃ śraddhāṃ tāmeva vidadhāmyaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whatever form (tanu) any devotee wishes to worship with faith (śraddhā), for each of them I make that very faith unwavering.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
sa tayā śraddhayā yuktastasyārādhanamīhate|
labhate ca tataḥ kāmānmayaiva vihitān hi tān
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Endowed with that faith he seeks to propitiate (ārādhana) that [form], and from it obtains his desires — which are in fact ordained by me alone.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
antavattu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tadbhavatyalpamedhasām|
devāndevayajo yānti madbhaktā yānti māmapi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: But the fruit of those of little understanding is finite (antavat); worshippers of the gods go to the gods, my devotees come to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
avyaktaṃ vyakitamāpannaṃ manyante māmabuddhayaḥ|
paraṃ bhāvamajānanto mamāvyayamanuttamam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The unintelligent (abuddhayaḥ) think of me, the unmanifest (avyakta), as one who has come into manifestation (vyakti), not knowing my higher state (paraṃ bhāvam), imperishable and unsurpassed.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Two readings: (a) they take him, who is unmanifest, to have (merely) become manifest like an ordinary embodied being; (b) they take him to have been unmanifest and to have now come into manifestation. Both agree that the error is not knowing his higher imperishable state. IAST 'vyakitam' is a transliteration artefact for vyaktim.

original.text:
nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogamāyāsamāvṛtaḥ|
mūḍho'yaṃ nābhijānāti loko māmajamavyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am not manifest (prakāśa) to all, being veiled by my yoga-māyā; this deluded world does not recognize me, the unborn (aja), the imperishable.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
vedāhaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna|
bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I know the beings that have passed, Arjuna, those that are present and those that are to come; but no one knows me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
icchādveṣasamutthena dvandvamohena bhārata|
sarvabhūtāni saṃmohaṃ sarge yānti parantapa
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Through the delusion of the pairs (dvandva-moha) arising from desire and aversion (icchā-dveṣa), Bhārata, all beings fall into bewilderment (saṃmoha) at birth / in creation (sarge), scorcher of foes.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'sarge' is read as 'at birth' or 'in (the course of) creation'.

original.text:
yeṣāṃ tvantagataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām|
te dvandvamohanirmuktā bhajante māṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: But those people of meritorious deeds (puṇya-karman) in whom sin (pāpa) has come to an end, freed from the delusion of the pairs, worship me firm in their vows (dṛḍha-vrata).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
jarāmaraṇamokṣāya māmāśritya yatanti ye|
te brahma tadviduḥ kṛtsnamadhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those who, taking refuge in me, strive for release from old age and death (jarā-maraṇa-mokṣa) know that Brahman, the whole of what pertains to the self (adhyātma), and action (karma) in its entirety.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ māṃ sādhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ|
prayāṇakāle'pi ca māṃ te viduryuktacetasaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those who know me together with what pertains to beings (adhibhūta) and to the gods (adhidaiva), and together with what pertains to sacrifice (adhiyajña) — they, with minds yoked (yukta-cetasaḥ), know me even at the time of departure (prayāṇa-kāla).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The six terms of 7.29–30 are the subject of Arjuna's questions at 8.1–2.

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa's teaching of knowledge with vijñāna of himself 'entire'. Movements: (1) 7.1–3 announcement — with mind attached to him and taking refuge, Arjuna will know him fully; knowledge with vijñāna after which nothing remains to be known; the rarity of those who know him in truth. (2) 7.4–7 his two natures: the lower eightfold prakṛti (five elements, mind, intellect, I-maker) and the higher prakṛti that has become the living being and upholds the world; both are the source of beings; he is the origin and dissolution of all; nothing is higher; all is strung on him like gems on a thread. (3) 7.8–12 he as the essence in things (taste in water, light of sun and moon, Oṃ in the Vedas, life, austerity, intelligence, strength, desire not opposed to dharma); the states of the three guṇas come from him, he is not in them, they in him. (4) 7.13–15 the world deluded by the guṇas does not know him; his divine guṇa-made māyā is crossed by those who take refuge in him; evil-doers of demonic disposition do not. (5) 7.16–19 four kinds of virtuous worshippers (distressed, seeker of knowledge, seeker of gain, knower); the knower, of single devotion, is foremost and held to be his very self; after many births the knower takes refuge, knowing 'Vāsudeva is all'. (6) 7.20–23 those driven by desires worship other deities; he makes their faith firm and grants the fruit, which is finite; god-worshippers go to the gods, his devotees to him. (7) 7.24–26 the unintelligent take the unmanifest as merely manifest; he is veiled by yoga-māyā; he knows all beings, none knows him. (8) 7.27–30 beings are bewildered by the pairs from birth; those whose sin has ended worship him; those striving for release from old age and death know Brahman, adhyātma and karma, and those who know him with adhibhūta, adhidaiva and adhiyajña know him even at death — terms that lead into chapter 8. Purpose as the chapter presents it: complete knowledge of the Lord, and refuge in him as the way across his māyā.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
kiṃ tadbrahma kimadhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣottama|
adhibhūtaṃ ca kiṃ proktamadhidaivaṃ kimucyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna asks: What is that Brahman? What is what pertains to the self (adhyātma)? What is action (karma), Supreme Person (puruṣottama)? And what is declared to be what pertains to beings (adhibhūta)? What is said to be what pertains to the gods (adhidaiva)?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Arjuna takes up the terms Kṛṣṇa used at 7.29–30; he addresses Kṛṣṇa as Puruṣottama.

original.text:
adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko'tra dehe'sminmadhusūdana|
prayāṇakāle ca kathaṃ jñeyo'si niyatātmabhiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna asks: Who, and how, is what pertains to sacrifice (adhiyajña) here in this body, Madhusūdana? And how are you to be known at the time of departure (prayāṇa-kāla) by those whose selves are controlled (niyatātman)?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
akṣaraṃ brahma paramaṃ svabhāvo'dhyātmamucyate|
bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargaḥ karmasaṃjñitaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa answers: Brahman is the supreme imperishable (akṣaraṃ paramam); its own being (svabhāva) is called adhyātma; the emission/offering (visarga) that brings about the coming-into-being of beings' existence is named action (karma).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'svabhāva' (own being) is read as Brahman's own presence as the inner self in each body, or as the individual self's own nature; 'visarga' is read as the sacrificial offering (release of oblation) that causes beings to arise, or as creative emission generally. The verse gives the definitions without explaining them.

original.text:
adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaścādhidaivatam|
adhiyajño'hamevātra dehe dehabhṛtāṃ vara
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: What pertains to beings (adhibhūta) is the perishable state (kṣaro bhāvaḥ); what pertains to the gods (adhidaivata) is the Person (puruṣa); what pertains to sacrifice (adhiyajña) is I myself, here in the body, best of the embodied.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The 'Person' (puruṣa) as adhidaivata is identified by commentators variously (e.g. the cosmic person / Hiraṇyagarbha, or the self as enjoyer); the verse names only 'puruṣa'. The adhiyajña is the Lord himself present 'here in the body'.

original.text:
antakāle ca māmeva smaranmuktvā kalevaram|
yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And whoever, at the time of the end (antakāla), departs leaving the body remembering me alone, comes to my state (mad-bhāva); there is no doubt of this.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram|
taṃ tamevaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whatever state/being (bhāva) one remembers when one finally leaves the body, to that very one he goes, Kaunteya, having always been shaped by that state (sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ' ties the last remembrance to what one has constantly dwelt on; hence 8.7 'at all times'.

original.text:
tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu māmanusmara yudhya ca|
mayyarpitamanobuddhirmāmevaiṣyasyasaṃśayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Therefore at all times remember me and fight; with mind and intellect offered to me (mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ), you will come to me alone, without doubt.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Remembrance is joined to Arjuna's own duty (fight); it is not presented as withdrawal from action.

original.text:
abhyāsayogayuktena cetasā nānyagāminā|
paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ yāti pārthānucintayan
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: With a mind yoked by the yoga of repeated practice (abhyāsa-yoga) and not straying elsewhere, meditating constantly (anucintayan), one goes to the supreme divine Person (paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyam), Pārtha.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
kaviṃ purāṇamanuśāsitāra
maṇoraṇīyāṃsamanusmaredyaḥ|
sarvasya dhātāramacintyarūpa
mādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whoever would meditate (anusmaret) on the seer (kavi), the ancient, the ruler (anuśāsitṛ), subtler than the subtle, the ordainer/supporter of all (sarvasya dhātṛ), of inconceivable form (acintya-rūpa), sun-coloured, beyond darkness (tamasaḥ parastāt) — [continued in 8.10]
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The epithets 'āditya-varṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt' and 'aṇor aṇīyāṃsam' echo Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 3.8 and Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.2.20. One sentence with 8.10.

original.text:
prayāṇakāle manasā'calena
bhaktyā yukto yogabalena caiva|
bhruvormadhye prāṇamāveśya samyak
sa taṃ paraṃ puruṣamupaiti divyam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — at the time of departure, with unmoving mind, yoked with devotion (bhakti) and by the power of yoga (yoga-bala), having made the breath (prāṇa) enter fully between the brows (bhruvor madhye), he reaches that supreme divine Person.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yadakṣaraṃ vedavido vadanti
viśanti yadyatayo vītarāgāḥ|
yadicchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti
tatte padaṃ saṃgraheṇa pravakṣye
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: That which the knowers of the Veda call the imperishable (akṣara), which ascetics (yati) free from passion enter, desiring which people practise the life of chastity/studentship (brahmacarya) — that state (pada) I will declare to you in brief.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Closely parallels Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.2.15 ('yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tat te padaṃ saṃgraheṇa bravīmi'), where the 'word/state' declared in brief is Oṃ; here the brief declaration follows in 8.12–13.

original.text:
sarvadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca|
mūrdhnyādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇamāsthito yogadhāraṇām
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Restraining all the gates [of the body] (sarva-dvārāṇi saṃyamya), confining the mind in the heart (hṛd), placing his breath (prāṇa) in the head (mūrdhan), established in yogic concentration (yoga-dhāraṇā) — [continued in 8.13]
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: One sentence with 8.13. The verse names no channel (nāḍī); compare the Upaniṣadic departure through the head (Chāndogya 8.6.6, Kaṭha 2.3.16), which the Gītā does not quote. 'Gates' are commonly taken as the sense-openings.

original.text:
omityekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharanmāmanusmaran|
yaḥ prayāti tyajandehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — uttering 'Oṃ', the one-syllabled Brahman (ekākṣaraṃ brahma), remembering me, whoever departs abandoning the body goes to the supreme goal (paramā gati).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Oṃ is called 'the one-syllabled Brahman' (cf. Kaṭha 1.2.16 'etad dhy evākṣaraṃ brahma'); uttering it is joined to remembering the Lord.

original.text:
ananyacetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ|
tasyāhaṃ sulabhaḥ pārtha nityayuktasya yoginaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For one who remembers me constantly, day after day, with mind on nothing else (ananya-cetāḥ) — for that ever-yoked yogin I am easy to reach (sulabha), Pārtha.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
māmupetya punarjanma duḥkhālayamaśāśvatam|
nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Having come to me, the great-souled (mahātman), who have reached the highest perfection (saṃsiddhi), do not come to rebirth (punar-janma), the abode of sorrow (duḥkha-ālaya), impermanent.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
ābrahmabhuvanāllokāḥ punarāvartino'rjuna|
māmupetya tu kaunteya punarjanma na vidyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The worlds up to Brahmā's world (ā-brahma-bhuvanāt) are subject to return (punar-āvartin), Arjuna; but having come to me, Kaunteya, there is no rebirth.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Even the highest world within the cosmos (Brahmā's) is a world of return; only reaching the Lord ends rebirth.

original.text:
sahasrayugaparyantamaharyadbrahmaṇo viduḥ|
rātriṃ yugasahasrāntāṃ te'horātravido janāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those who know the day of Brahmā as lasting a thousand ages (yuga), and his night as ending after a thousand ages — they are people who know day and night.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Nearly the same wording is found in Manusmṛti 1.72–73 (numbering of that parallel not checked here). The 'ages' are taken by commentators as full four-age cycles.

original.text:
avyaktādvyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavantyaharāgame|
rātryāgame pralīyante tatraivāvyaktasaṃjñake
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: At the coming of [Brahmā's] day all manifest things (vyaktayaḥ) come forth from the unmanifest (avyakta); at the coming of night they dissolve into that very thing called the unmanifest.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
bhūtagrāmaḥ sa evāyaṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate|
rātryāgame'vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavatyaharāgame
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: This same multitude of beings (bhūta-grāma), coming to be again and again, dissolves helplessly (avaśa) at the coming of night, Pārtha, and comes forth at the coming of day.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
parastasmāttu bhāvo'nyo'vyakto'vyaktātsanātanaḥ|
yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: But beyond that unmanifest there is another, unmanifest, eternal (sanātana) being (bhāva), which does not perish when all beings perish.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Distinguishes two 'unmanifests': the cosmic unmanifest into which beings dissolve (8.18) and a higher eternal unmanifest that does not perish.

original.text:
avyakto'kṣara ityuktastamāhuḥ paramāṃ gatim|
yaṃ prāpya na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: That unmanifest is called the imperishable (akṣara); they call it the supreme goal (paramā gati); having reached it they do not return — that is my supreme abode (dhāma paramaṃ mama).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyastvananyayā|
yasyāntaḥsthāni bhūtāni yena sarvamidaṃ tatam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: That supreme Person (puruṣaḥ paraḥ), Pārtha, is to be gained by undivided devotion (bhaktyā ananyayā) — he within whom beings abide, by whom all this is pervaded (tatam).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yatra kāle tvanāvṛttimāvṛttiṃ caiva yoginaḥ|
prayātā yānti taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Now I will tell you the time (kāla) at which yogins, departing, go to non-return (anāvṛtti) and to return (āvṛtti), bull of the Bharatas.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'kāla' (time) is taken by some commentators as the path marked by presiding deities of time rather than the literal moment of death; the verse says 'time'.

original.text:
agnirjyotirahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam|
tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Fire, light, day, the bright [fortnight] (śukla), the six months of the northern course (uttarāyaṇa): departing there, people who know Brahman (brahma-vidaḥ) go to Brahman.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Stations of the bright path as in the Upaniṣadic path of the gods (Chāndogya 5.10.1–2; Bṛhadāraṇyaka 6.2.15). Commentators divide on whether the stations are times of death or deities conducting the departed, and on which Brahman is reached.

original.text:
dhūmo rātristathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam|
tatra cāndramasaṃ jyotiryogī prāpya nivartate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Smoke, night, likewise the dark [fortnight] (kṛṣṇa), the six months of the southern course (dakṣiṇāyana): there the yogin reaches the lunar light (cāndramasaṃ jyotiḥ) and returns.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Stations of the dark path as in the Upaniṣadic path of the fathers. The verse says 'the yogin'; commentators take this as the performer of rites with desire for results.

original.text:
śuklakṛṣṇe gatī hyete jagataḥ śāśvate mate|
ekayā yātyanāvṛttimanyayā''vartate punaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: These two courses, the bright and the dark (śukla-kṛṣṇe gatī), are held to be everlasting for the world; by the one a person goes to non-return, by the other he returns again.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
naite sṛtī pārtha jānanyogī muhyati kaścana|
tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu yogayukto bhavārjuna
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Knowing these two paths (sṛti), Pārtha, no yogin is deluded; therefore at all times be yoked in yoga (yoga-yukta), Arjuna.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva
dāneṣu yatpuṇyaphalaṃ pradiṣṭam|
atyeti tatsarvamidaṃ viditvā
yogī paraṃ sthānamupaiti cādyam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whatever fruit of merit (puṇya-phala) is declared for the Vedas, for sacrifices, austerities and gifts — the yogin who knows this passes beyond all of it and reaches the supreme, primal place (paraṃ sthānam ādyam).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'idaṃ viditvā' — having known 'this' (the teaching of the chapter, answering 8.1–2).

paraphrase: Answers to Arjuna's questions about the terms of 7.29–30 and about knowing the Lord at death; the imperishable (akṣara) as the goal. Movements: (1) 8.1–2 Arjuna asks what Brahman, adhyātma, karma, adhibhūta, adhidaiva and adhiyajña are, and how the Lord is known at the time of departure. (2) 8.3–4 definitions: Brahman is the supreme imperishable, adhyātma its own being, karma the emission that brings beings into existence, adhibhūta the perishable state, adhidaivata the Person, adhiyajña the Lord himself in the body. (3) 8.5–8 whoever dies remembering him comes to his state; one goes to whatever one remembers at the end, as habitually dwelt on; so remember him always and fight; constant practice leads to the supreme Person. (4) 8.9–13 the dying yogin's meditation: on the ancient seer beyond darkness, with breath between the brows; the imperishable 'state' declared in brief; restraining the gates, mind in the heart, breath in the head, uttering Oṃ and remembering him, one reaches the supreme goal. (5) 8.14–16 he is easy to reach for the constant rememberer; those who reach him are not reborn, whereas all worlds up to Brahmā's return. (6) 8.17–22 Brahmā's day and night of a thousand ages; beings manifest from and dissolve into the unmanifest; beyond it another eternal unmanifest, called the imperishable, the supreme goal and his supreme abode, reached by undivided devotion to the all-pervading Person. (7) 8.23–27 the two courses of the departed: the bright (fire, light, day, bright fortnight, northern half-year) leading to Brahman without return, the dark (smoke, night, dark fortnight, southern half-year) leading to the lunar light and return; the yogin who knows them is not deluded. (8) 8.28 the yogin who knows this passes beyond all merit of Veda, sacrifice, austerity and gift to the supreme primal place.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
idaṃ tu te guhyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmyanasūyave|
jñānaṃ vijñānasahitaṃ yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: To you, who do not cavil (anasūyu), I will declare this most secret (guhyatama) knowledge (jñāna) together with vijñāna; knowing it you will be freed from what is inauspicious (aśubha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The hearer's qualification is freedom from cavilling (anasūyā); cf. 18.67, which forbids telling the teaching to one who cavils at the Lord. Stated result: release from the inauspicious.

original.text:
rājavidyā rājaguhyaṃ pavitramidamuttamam|
pratyakṣāvagamaṃ dharmyaṃ susukhaṃ kartumavyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: It is the royal knowledge (rāja-vidyā), the royal secret (rāja-guhya), the supreme purifier; it is known by direct apprehension (pratyakṣa-avagama), in accord with dharma (dharmya), very easy to practise, and imperishable.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Praise of the teaching (arthavāda in the Mīmāṃsā sense). 'rāja-vidyā, rāja-guhya' are read as 'king of knowledges, king of secrets' or 'knowledge/secret of kings'.

original.text:
aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa|
aprāpya māṃ nivartante mṛtyusaṃsāravartmani
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: People who have no faith (aśraddadhāna) in this dharma, scorcher of foes, not reaching me, return to the path of death and saṃsāra (mṛtyu-saṃsāra-vartman).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
mayā tatamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadavyaktamūrtinā|
matsthāni sarvabhūtāni na cāhaṃ teṣvavasthitaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: All this world is pervaded (tata) by me in my unmanifest form (avyakta-mūrti); all beings abide in me, but I am not established in them.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
na ca matsthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogamaiśvaram|
bhūtabhṛnna ca bhūtastho mamātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And yet beings do not abide in me — behold my lordly yoga (yogam aiśvaram)! Sustaining beings (bhūta-bhṛt) and not abiding in beings, my self (ātman) brings beings into being (bhūta-bhāvana).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Stands in deliberate tension with 9.4 ('all beings abide in me'); the verse itself presents the two statements as the Lord's 'lordly yoga' and does not resolve them. Commentators resolve it differently (e.g. by the Lord's non-attachment/non-contact, or by the difference between upholding and being contained).

original.text:
yathā''kāśasthito nityaṃ vāyuḥ sarvatrago mahān|

kalpakṣaye punastāni kalpādau visṛjāmyaham

bhūtagrāmamimaṃ kṛtsnamavaśaṃ prakṛtervaśāt
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

original.text:

udāsīnavadāsīnamasaktaṃ teṣu karmasu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ|
rākṣasīmāsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
mahātmānastu māṃ pārtha daivīṃ prakṛtimāśritāḥ|
bhajantyananyamanaso jñātvā bhūtādimavyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: But the great-souled (mahātman), Pārtha, resorting to the divine nature (daivī prakṛti), worship me with minds on nothing else (ananya-manas), knowing me as the imperishable origin of beings (bhūtādi).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
satataṃ kīrtayanto māṃ yatantaśca dṛḍhavratāḥ|
namasyantaśca māṃ bhaktyā nityayuktā upāsate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Always glorifying me (kīrtayantaḥ), striving, firm in their vows (dṛḍha-vrata), and bowing to me (namasyantaḥ) with devotion, ever yoked, they worship me (upāsate).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Continues the description of the great-souled of 9.13.

original.text:
jñānayajñena cāpyanye yajanto māmupāsate|
ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvatomukham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Others too, sacrificing with the sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña), worship me — as one (ekatvena), as distinct (pṛthaktvena), in many ways (bahudhā) — me who face in all directions (viśvato-mukha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Commentators divide on 'as one, as distinct, in many ways' (e.g. worship of the Lord as identical with oneself, as other than oneself, or in his many forms; or as the one whose body is the manifold world). The verse lists the modes without ranking them.

original.text:
ahaṃ kraturahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhā'hamahamauṣadham|
maṃtro'hamahamevājyamahamagnirahaṃ hutam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am the rite (kratu), I am the sacrifice (yajña), I am the offering to the ancestors (svadhā), I am the healing plant (auṣadha); I am the mantra, I am the clarified butter (ājya), I am the fire (agni), I am the oblation offered (huta).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Every element of the sacrifice is identified with the Lord (cf. 4.24).

original.text:
pitā'hamasya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ|
vedyaṃ pavitramoṃkāra ṛk sāma yajureva ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am the father of this world, the mother, the ordainer (dhātṛ), the grandsire; what is to be known (vedya), the purifier, the syllable Oṃ (oṃkāra), and the Ṛk, the Sāman and the Yajus.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
gatirbhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṃ suhṛt|
prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījamavyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: [I am] the goal (gati), the upholder (bhartṛ), the lord (prabhu), the witness (sākṣin), the dwelling (nivāsa), the refuge (śaraṇa), the friend (suhṛd); the origin (prabhava), the dissolution (pralaya), the ground (sthāna), the treasure-house (nidhāna), the imperishable seed (bījam avyayam).

original.text:
tapāmyahamahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmyutsṛjāmi ca|
amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuśca sadasaccāhamarjuna
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I give heat; I hold back and send forth the rain; I am immortality (amṛta) and death (mṛtyu), being (sat) and non-being (asat), Arjuna.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
traividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūtapāpā
yajñairiṣṭvā svargatiṃ prārthayante|
te puṇyamāsādya surendraloka
maśnanti divyāndivi devabhogān
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Knowers of the three Vedas (traividya), drinkers of soma, cleansed of sin, worshipping me with sacrifices, pray for the way to heaven (svar-gati); reaching the holy world of the lord of the gods (surendra-loka), they enjoy in heaven the divine enjoyments of the gods.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
te taṃ bhuktvā svargalokaṃ viśālaṃ
kṣīṇe puṇye martyalokaṃ viśanti|
eva trayīdharmamanuprapannā
gatāgataṃ kāmakāmā labhante
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Having enjoyed that vast heavenly world, when their merit (puṇya) is exhausted they enter the world of mortals; thus following the dharma of the three Vedas (trayī-dharma), desiring objects of desire (kāma-kāma), they obtain going and coming (gatāgata).

original.text:
ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate|
teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those people who, with no other [object] (ananya), think of me and worship me all around (paryupāsate) — for them, ever devoted (nitya-abhiyukta), I carry (vahāmi) acquisition and preservation (yoga-kṣema).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'yoga-kṣema': acquiring what is not had and preserving what is had; the Lord himself carries it for the undivided devotee.

original.text:
ye'pyanyadevatā bhaktā yajante śraddhayā'nvitāḥ|
te'pi māmeva kaunteya yajantyavidhipūrvakam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhureva ca|
na tu māmabhijānanti tattvenātaścyavanti te
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For I am the enjoyer (bhoktṛ) and the lord (prabhu) of all sacrifices; but they do not recognize me in truth (tattvena), and therefore they fall.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
yānti devavratā devān pitṛ़nyānti pitṛvratāḥ|
bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti madyājino'pi mām
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those vowed to the gods (deva-vrata) go to the gods; those vowed to the ancestors (pitṛ-vrata) go to the ancestors; those who offer to spirits/beings (bhūtejya) go to the beings; and those who sacrifice to me come to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati|
tadahaṃ bhaktyupahṛtamaśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water — that, offered with devotion (bhakti-upahṛta) by one whose self is pure/controlled (prayatātman), I partake of (aśnāmi).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
yatkaroṣi yadaśnāsi yajjuhoṣi dadāsi yat|
yattapasyasi kaunteya tatkuruṣva madarpaṇam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practise, Kaunteya — do that as an offering to me (mad-arpaṇa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
śubhāśubhaphalairevaṃ mokṣyase karmabandhanaiḥ|
saṃnyāsayogayuktātmā vimukto māmupaiṣyasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Thus you will be freed from the bonds of action (karma-bandhana) with their good and bad fruits; with your self yoked in the yoga of renunciation (saṃnyāsa-yoga), freed, you will come to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
samo'haṃ sarvabhūteṣu na me dveṣyo'sti na priyaḥ|
ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpyaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

original.text:
api cetsudurācāro bhajate māmananyabhāk|
sādhureva sa mantavyaḥ samyagvyavasito hi saḥ

original.text:
kṣipraṃ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvacchāntiṃ nigacchati|
kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Quickly he becomes righteous (dharmātman) and attains lasting peace (śāśvatī śānti). Kaunteya, proclaim it: my devotee does not perish.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'pratijānīhi' — Kṛṣṇa bids Arjuna declare (make a pledge) that the devotee never perishes.

original.text:
māṃ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye'pi syuḥ pāpayonayaḥ|
striyo vaiśyāstathā śūdrāste'pi yānti parāṃ gatim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For those who take refuge in me, Pārtha, even though they may be of sinful birth (pāpa-yoni) — women, vaiśyas and also śūdras — they too go to the highest goal (parā gati).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Grammatically 'pāpa-yonayaḥ' may stand in apposition to 'women, vaiśyas and śūdras' or name a separate group (those of sinful birth) alongside them; commentators take both lines. Either way the verse's claim is that taking refuge in the Lord brings all of them to the highest goal.

original.text:
kiṃ punarbrāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayastathā|
anityamasukhaṃ lokamimaṃ prāpya bhajasva mām
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: How much more, then, holy brāhmaṇas and devoted royal seers (rāja-ṛṣi)! Having come into this impermanent, joyless world, worship me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The a fortiori argument continues 9.32; the closing half-verse turns to Arjuna (a royal seer by birth) with the injunction to worship.

original.text:
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru|
māmevaiṣyasi yuktvaivamātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Be one whose mind is on me (man-manāḥ), my devotee (mad-bhakta), my worshipper (mad-yājin); bow to me (namas-kuru). Having thus yoked yourself, with me as your final aim (mat-parāyaṇa), you will come to me alone.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The first line is repeated verbatim at 18.65 (repetition, abhyāsa).

paraphrase: The 'royal knowledge, royal secret': the Lord's pervasion and transcendence of the world, and devotion as the way open to all. Movements: (1) 9.1–3 the most secret knowledge with vijñāna, for one free of cavilling; praised as royal knowledge, purifying, directly known, easy; those without faith return to death and saṃsāra. (2) 9.4–10 the Lord pervades all in unmanifest form; beings abide in him but he not in them — and yet beings do not abide in him: his lordly yoga; the wind in space as illustration; at the end of a kalpa beings enter his prakṛti and he sends them forth again; those acts do not bind him, seated as if indifferent; prakṛti produces the world under his oversight. (3) 9.11–15 the deluded, of demonic nature, disregard him in human form; the great-souled of divine nature worship him with undivided mind, glorifying and bowing, or through the sacrifice of knowledge as one, distinct and many. (4) 9.16–19 he is every element of the sacrifice, father and mother of the world, Oṃ and the three Vedas, goal, witness, refuge, friend, origin and dissolution, immortality and death, being and non-being. (5) 9.20–25 Vedic ritualists win heaven and return when merit is spent; the undivided devotee's welfare he carries himself; worship of other deities reaches him but not by the rule; each goes to what he worships. (6) 9.26–34 the simplest offering (leaf, flower, fruit, water) is accepted; doing all as an offering to him frees from the bonds of action; he is the same to all yet devotees are in him and he in them; even one of very bad conduct who worships undividedly is to be counted good and does not perish; women, vaiśyas, śūdras and those of sinful birth reach the highest goal by refuge in him; closing injunction: mind on me, my devotee, my worshipper, bow to me, you will come to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
